comments.content: The `matches` method signature changed from `matches(String name)` to `matches(String... names)`. This is a breaking API change for any external implementations or callers. Consider adding a new method (e.g., `matchesAny`) instead of changing the existing one, or at minimum add `@Deprecated` to the old signature and provide a default implementation.

The new `atLeastOneNameMatchesPattern` method uses `Arrays.stream(names)` which will throw NullPointerException if `names` is null. The caller `matches(String... names)` can receive null (varargs can be null). Add a null check at the start of `matches` or in `atLeastOneNameMatchesPattern`.

The call `filter.matches(objectName, overloadedObject.getOverloadedName())` passes two arguments, but `DBSObjectFilter.matches` now accepts varargs `String...`. This works but the intent is clearer if you pass an array explicitly: `filter.matches(new String[]{objectName, overloadedObject.getOverloadedName()})`. Also, `overloadedObject.getOverloadedName()` could return null - the filter should handle null names gracefully (see previous comment about NPE).
